q7.answer: Progress is stored in the Kafka consumer group offsets, one group per target index (search-indexer-INDEX). It advances to the last batch offset + 1, and only once every item in the batch is resolved: acknowledged by the index, counted as a stale version conflict, or acknowledged as produced to the DLQ.

q8.answer: It resumes from the last committed offset and replays that partition in order. The commit_lsn versions turn replayed writes into stale conflicts or idempotent rewrites. The one known gap: if the store has already purged a delete tombstone, a product can briefly reappear until its delete is replayed.

q9.answer: Before the snapshot opens, the rebuild records the end offsets of all 12 partitions and then S_low. Once the backfill is fully acknowledged, the consumer group for the new index starts at those recorded offsets and replays everything. Changes at or after S_low overwrite snapshot rows in per-id commit order, and older changes conflict as stale.

q10.answer: Every bulk-copied document carries S_low as its version. S_low is pg_current_wal_lsn, recorded after the partition offsets and before the repeatable-read snapshot begins. A resumed snapshot keeps the same S_low.

q11.answer: Both consumer groups keep running for 48 hours, so the old index still receives every change, and switching back is one atomic alias call that loses nothing. The window ends after 48 hours with no rollback: the old index's consumer group is stopped and deleted, then the old index is deleted. I never decided what happens to the new index and its group after a rollback.

q12.answer: Search is unaffected because the alias never moves until the gate passes, so the old index keeps serving. After a data-loss trigger it serves with gaps. A lost snapshot resumes from the last acknowledged id in a new snapshot, keeping S_low and the start offsets. A catch-up that stalls keeps rechecking the gate and raises an alert after 1 hour. An abandoned rebuild is cleaned up by deleting the new index and its consumer group.
